notes:
User is an active bird enthusiast interested in birdwatching, bird photography, and identifying confusing warblers and sparrows. They photograph with telephoto equipment; specific camera and lens details remain unknown. They regularly visit a local park and keep a species list; after seeing a Northern Flicker last weekend, their total reached 32 species. They use eBird to organize sightings and submit observations and value seeing reports from other local birders. They are also interested in finding nearby reserves, parks, and bird-diverse habitats.

They plan a bird-friendly picnic in the local park this weekend. Intended attractants include sunflower seeds, suet, peanut butter, and fresh fruit (especially apples and oranges), plus water and a portable birdbath or bubbler. They are considering creamy versus crunchy peanut butter and sliced versus whole fruit. They hope suet and peanut butter will attract woodpeckers and nuthatches, including possible Downy, Hairy, Red-bellied, or Pileated Woodpeckers depending on local species and habitat. They will bring binoculars to look closely for warblers and sparrows, planning to scan dense foliage for active warblers and grassy/weedy areas for sparrows.

Helpful guidance: check park feeding rules; do not litter; use clean trays or proper feeders; keep food fresh and clean water frequently changed; provide shallow water (about 2–3 inches), preferably moving/oxygenated, with partial shade and protection from wind. Avoid leaving sticky peanut butter exposed on ordinary surfaces; use a suitable feeder. Fruit should be cut into manageable pieces, with seeds, pits, and apple cores removed. Fresh, clean water is preferable to stagnant water, but birds can still use a simple shallow dish. Maintain distance and avoid disturbing wildlife. Future location-specific reserve recommendations will require the user’s geographic area.
